system.concept: Toreador patron of the arts, the last Western Kindred still openly promoting Hong Kong's cultural scene
system.biography:
Background

An aspiring Edinburgh composer and performer frustrated by her era's dismissal of female musicians, Gwendolyn Fleming was Embraced by the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} noble Malcolm McCluan, Lord Blackloch. The pair traveled Europe and America chasing culture for a century before arriving in Hong Kong in 1901. Malcolm found the city barbarous and eventually returned to Europe, but Gwendolyn was enraptured by Hong Kong's vitality and Chinese opera, and the split with her sire was amicable. She built her reputation as one of the city's leading patrons of the arts, discovering and sponsoring both Chinese and European talent. When the rest of Hong Kong's Toreador fled ahead of the 1997 handover, Gwendolyn alone remained, determined to be the last bastion of Western culture in the city and to eventually forge ties with the Kuei-jin to blend Eastern and Western art.

Image

A slender, breathtakingly beautiful young woman in her apparent 20s, dressed in the latest European fashion accented with jade jewelry; chestnut curls frame pale-green eyes.

Roleplaying Hints

Utterly absorbed in fathoming Chinese music and opera; plans to bide her time through the initial upheaval of Chinese rule before reaching out to the Cathayan cultural community, confident they will recognize her sincerity.

Haven

A lavish mansion on the Peak with an attached concert hall and theater; her resting place lies in a crypt cut into the mountainside beneath it.
system.notes: Disciplines (as printed): Auspex 4, Celerity 3, Fortitude 2, Presence 4, Protean 3. Sire: Malcolm McCluan, Lord Blackloch (returned to Europe; the parting was amicable).

vtmlarp.source: World of Darkness: Hong Kong (Hong Kong by Night), Chapter Four: The Spirits' Children
